notes: Curated questions. 'families' ['*'] = any role. Each item carries its assessment purpose. Generated questions are stored in the DB `questions` table, not here.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you took ownership of a problem that wasn't strictly yours to solve. What did you do?
probes: Why did you step in rather than escalate?
What exactly did you do in the first week?
What changed because of it?

questions.text: Tell me about a decision you made that turned out to be wrong. What was your reasoning at the time, and what did you change afterwards?
questions.intent: Reflection and learning from own mistakes.
probes: What information did you not have?
What signal did you ignore?
Where have you applied this since?

questions.text: Describe a real disagreement you had with a manager or senior colleague about how to do something. How did it play out?
probes: What was their strongest argument?
How did you raise it?
Looking back, who was right?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to get people who didn't report to you to do something they initially resisted.
probes: What was the real reason for the resistance?
What did you do differently for the toughest person?
What would have happened if you hadn't?

questions.text: What is the most measurable impact you've had in a role or project so far, and how do you know it was your doing?
strong: baseline + delta + why it is attributable
probes: What was the baseline?
What else changed in the same period?
How much of that would have happened anyway?

questions.text: Tell me about a period when you had more to do than time allowed. What did you deliver, what did you drop, and how did you decide?
strong: names what was dropped and why
probes: Who was unhappy with what you dropped?
Would you make the same call today?

questions.text: What is the most useful piece of critical feedback you've received, and what did you change because of it?
questions.intent: Openness to feedback and behaviour change.
weak: feedback that is a disguised strength
probes: How did you react at first?
How would someone know you've changed?

questions.text: Describe a situation where two stakeholders wanted conflicting things from you. How did you handle it?
probes: What did each actually need?
Who lost out, and how did you tell them?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to make progress on a problem with very little information or direction.
evidence: what they did to reduce uncertainty
probes: What was your first step and why?
Which assumption turned out wrong?

questions.text: Tell me about a time a teammate was struggling and it was affecting your work. What did you do?
probes: What did you say to them?
What would you do if it didn't improve?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to deal with persistent under-performance in your team.
probes: What did you think was causing it?
What did you say in the first conversation?
How long did you give it?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you were under pressure to cut a corner. What did you do?
strong: held the line with a practical alternative
probes: What would have happened if you had cut it?
Who did you involve?

questions.text: Why this role, and why now? Walk me through how your experience so far leads here.
evidence: link between past and this role
strong: specific to this role and company
probes: What would make this role a mistake for you?
What else are you considering?

questions.text: What do you expect a typical week in this role to look like, and which part do you think you'll find hardest?
probes: Why that part?
What have you done to prepare for it?

questions.text: Looking at your career choices so far, which one would you make differently, and why?
probes: What did you know then that pushed you that way?

questions.text: It's Thursday. Your manager wants an analysis by Monday, and a key client escalates an issue that will take most of your Friday. What do you do?
weak: plans to work all weekend without telling anyone
probes: What do you say to your manager, and when?
What if the client issue takes longer?

questions.text: You discover an error in a report you sent to senior leadership yesterday, and it changes one of the conclusions. What do you do next?
probes: Who do you tell first?
How do you stop it happening again?

questions.text: A colleague keeps missing their part of a shared deliverable and the deadline is three days away. What do you do?
questions.intent: Direct, constructive handling of a delivery risk.
strong: direct conversation plus a contingency plan
probes: What if they say they're overloaded by another manager?

questions.text: You're asked to deliver a result you believe isn't achievable with the resources you've been given. How do you respond?
questions.intent: Pushing back with evidence and options.
strong: quantifies the gap and offers options
probes: How would you show the gap?
Which option would you recommend?

questions.text: A regional chain of 40 budget hotels has seen profits fall about 20% over two years while occupancy stayed flat. How would you approach this?
strong: notes flat occupancy points to rate or cost
probes: Average room rate fell 12% while costs rose 5%. What does that tell you?
What would you check next?
What do you recommend?

questions.text: An electric-scooter maker wants to enter a new Tier-2 city. What would you need to know before recommending yes or no?
strong: tailored to EV and Tier-2 specifics (charging, financing, service)
probes: Which factor is most likely to kill the case?
How would you size the market?

questions.text: Estimate the annual market for packaged drinking water in a metro city of about 10 million people.
probes: Which assumption drives the answer most?
How would you sanity-check it?

questions.text: After three weeks of analysis, you've found the client's flagship product is losing money. You have five minutes with their CEO. How do you structure that conversation?
questions.intent: Answer-first synthesis to a senior stakeholder.
probes: The CEO launched that product personally. Does that change anything?
What's your one-sentence opener?

questions.text: When you have limited time on a project, how do you decide which hypothesis to test first?
probes: Give me an example where you got the order wrong.

questions.text: Your client counterpart disagrees with your team's main finding and says they'll escalate to their boss. What do you do?
strong: re-tests the finding and engages the objection
probes: What if they're right about one part?

questions.text: How would you structure the question: should a mid-sized bank launch its own digital-only brand?
probes: What's the single biggest risk?
What would make you say no?

questions.text: Pick a company you know well. Where should it play over the next three years, and what should it stop doing?
probes: What would a competitor do in response?
What evidence would change your view?

questions.text: How would you evaluate whether to build a capability in-house or acquire a company that already has it?
strong: integration risk and strategic control considered
probes: What usually goes wrong after the acquisition?

questions.text: If a company's depreciation expense increases by 10 crore, walk me through how that flows through the three financial statements. Assume a 25% tax rate.
probes: Why does cash go up?
What if the asset was leased instead?

questions.text: A profitable company is running out of cash. What are the likely reasons, and how would you diagnose it?
probes: Receivable days went from 45 to 75. What do you do?

questions.text: How would you estimate the cost of capital for an unlisted company, and which input are you least confident about?
probes: How would you choose comparables?

questions.text: Two projects: one has a higher IRR, the other a higher NPV. Which do you choose, and why?
evidence: scale and timing issues of IRR
weak: picks IRR because it's a percentage
probes: When might you still prefer the higher IRR?

questions.text: Revenue came in 8% below budget this quarter but EBITDA was on target. What questions would you ask to explain that?
probes: Which would worry you most for next quarter?

questions.text: How do you make a financial model you've built trustworthy enough for someone else to rely on?
probes: Tell me about an error you caught in a model.

questions.text: Walk me through a DCF, and then tell me which input you'd challenge first in someone else's model and why.
strong: challenges terminal value or growth with reason
probes: Terminal value is 80% of the value. Is that a problem?

questions.text: When would you trust a comparable-companies valuation more than a DCF, and when less?
probes: Which multiple would you use for a loss-making company?

questions.text: Explain how a bond's price responds to a rise in interest rates, and why a longer-duration bond moves more.
probes: What about a zero-coupon bond?

questions.text: An investor buys a put option on a stock they already own. What are they protecting against, and what does it cost them?
probes: What drives the premium?

questions.text: Pitch me a stock or a company you'd invest in. What is the market missing?
probes: What would make you wrong?
What's the catalyst?

questions.text: How would a strategic buyer and a private-equity buyer think differently about the price they can pay for the same company?
probes: What limits what PE can pay?

questions.text: A mid-sized manufacturer wants a working-capital loan. Which three numbers would you look at first, and why?
strong: explains why each matters for repayment
probes: Interest cover is 1.4x. What now?

questions.text: What makes a loan covenant useful to a lender, and how can it backfire?
probes: Give an example of a bad covenant.

questions.text: How would you assess the risk of a portfolio of small-business loans going into a slowdown?
probes: Which segment breaks first?

questions.text: A software company bills a customer upfront for a three-year contract. How should it recognise that revenue, and why?
probes: What if part of the fee is for one-time setup?

questions.text: During an audit you find a material expense recorded in the wrong period. What do you do?
probes: Management refuses to adjust. Now what?

questions.text: How would you test whether a company's reported inventory figure is reasonable?
probes: Inventory days rose sharply. What does that suggest?

questions.text: Tell me about a consumer insight that changed a decision you were involved in. How did you find it, and how did you know it was an insight rather than just an observation?
probes: What did you do with it?
How did you validate it?

questions.text: Pick a brand you think is poorly positioned. Who should it be for, what should it stand for, and what would you change first?
probes: What would you lose by narrowing the target?

questions.text: A campaign coincided with a 30% spike in sales during its run. How would you tell whether it actually worked?
probes: Sales dropped below baseline the month after. What does that mean?

questions.text: A competitor cuts prices by 10% in your core category. What do you do, and what would you look at before deciding?
probes: Your share drops 2 points in a month. Now?

questions.text: How would you launch a premium variant of an existing mass-market product without hurting the core brand?
probes: Which channel first and why?

questions.text: How would you decide whether to spend the next rupee on consumer advertising or on trade promotions?
probes: What data would settle it?

questions.text: You have two weeks and a small budget to understand why repeat purchase dropped. How would you design the research?
strong: uses existing data then targeted qual
probes: Who exactly would you talk to?

questions.text: Your customer acquisition cost has doubled over six months while conversion is flat. Where do you look?
probes: One channel's CPM rose 60%. What next?

questions.text: How would you diagnose a drop in 30-day retention for a consumer app?
probes: Only users from one channel dropped. What does that tell you?

questions.text: Design an experiment to test whether a new onboarding flow improves activation. What could make the result misleading?
probes: How long would you run it?

questions.text: You take over a territory where primary sales are on target but secondary sales are falling. What's happening, and what do you do?
probes: Distributor stock is at 45 days. What now?

questions.text: Your biggest distributor threatens to stop stocking your products unless you raise his margin by 2%. How do you handle it?
probes: He gives you until Friday. What do you prepare?

questions.text: Tell me about a sales target you missed. What happened, and what did you change?
probes: When did you know you'd miss it?

questions.text: If you need to close 10 deals this quarter, how do you work backwards to the activity you need?
probes: Your win rate drops from 25% to 15%. What changes?

questions.text: Tell me about a negotiation where you got a better outcome without giving a discount.
probes: What was your walk-away point?

questions.text: How would you decide which retail outlets in your territory to visit weekly and which monthly?
probes: A small outlet is growing fast. Where does it go?

questions.text: A key account's new purchasing head wants to cut the number of suppliers. What's your plan?
probes: Who else in the account would you meet?

questions.text: It's the last week of the month, you're 15% short of target, and a dealer offers to take extra stock if you extend his credit by 30 days. What do you do?
strong: weighs inventory and credit risk, escalates transparently
probes: Your manager says 'just do it'. Now?

questions.text: Pick a product you use often. Who is it for, what problem does it solve badly, and how would you improve it?
probes: How would you know your change worked?
What would you not build?

questions.text: Daily active users of a food-delivery app dropped 10% week over week. How would you investigate?
probes: It's only on Android in two cities. What next?

questions.text: You can fund one of three things: a top customer's feature request, a fix for a bug affecting 5% of users, and an experiment your data says could lift conversion. How do you decide?
probes: The customer is 15% of revenue. Does that change it?

questions.text: Tell me about a product you shipped. What did you cut from scope to ship it, and how did you decide?
probes: Did you add any of it back later?

questions.text: How would you measure the success of a new 'save for later' feature in a shopping app?
strong: links usage to conversion with guardrail
probes: Saves go up but conversion falls. Why might that be?

questions.text: Tell me about a time engineering told you your requirement wasn't feasible in the timeline. What happened?
probes: What did you learn about how to write requirements?

questions.text: A plant is missing its daily output target by 12% even though every machine is running. How would you find the constraint?
probes: Station 3 has 20% scrap. What now?

questions.text: Tell me about a process you improved. How did you measure before and after?
probes: Did it hold six months later?

questions.text: How would you reduce delivery delays in a last-mile network without adding riders?
probes: Which would you test first?

questions.text: How would you decide how much safety stock to hold for a product with volatile demand?
probes: Lead time doubles. What changes?

questions.text: Demand forecasts have been 25% off for three months in a row. What do you do?
probes: Sales keeps over-forecasting. How do you handle it?

questions.text: A key supplier says raw-material costs force a 12% price increase. How do you approach it?
strong: validates with cost breakdown and indices
probes: The index rose 6%. What's your counter?

questions.text: An employee complains that their manager is treating them unfairly. Walk me through what you would do.
probes: The manager is the top performer in the region. Does that change anything?

questions.text: Attrition in one sales team is double the company average. How would you find out why?
probes: Most exits are in the first 6 months. What does that suggest?

questions.text: How would you design an interview process for a role so that it is both rigorous and fair?
probes: How would you check it's working?

questions.text: A high performer is creating friction in the team and the manager wants to ignore it. What do you advise?
strong: addresses behaviour with the manager and the person
probes: The manager pushes back. What do you say?

questions.text: How would you decide whether to match a counter-offer for a key employee?
probes: Matching would put them above their manager. Now?

questions.text: When would you choose a hash map over a balanced binary search tree, and what do you give up?
probes: You need range queries. Which now?

questions.text: How would you find the first non-repeating character in a very large stream of characters? Talk me through the approach, complexity and edge cases.
strong: O(1) per char with ordered structure
probes: What if the alphabet is all of Unicode?

questions.text: Design a URL-shortening service. Start with requirements and expected scale.
probes: How do you avoid collisions?
Reads are 100x writes. What changes?

questions.text: An API endpoint that was fast yesterday now takes several seconds for some users only. How do you investigate?
strong: isolates by segment and recent change
probes: Only users with large accounts are slow. What next?

questions.text: How do you decide what to cover with unit tests and what with integration tests?
probes: Give me a bug a unit test would never catch.

questions.text: Two requests try to update the same account balance at the same time. What can go wrong, and how do you prevent it?
strong: names lost update and a concrete fix
probes: The two requests hit different servers. Does your fix still work?

questions.text: Tell me about the most technically complex thing you've built. Which design decision are you least sure about now?
weak: describes the team's system without own role
probes: What would you change if traffic grew 10x?

questions.text: How do database indexes speed up reads, and what do they cost?
probes: When would the planner ignore your index?

questions.text: You join orders to customers and the revenue total comes out higher than finance's number. What are the likely causes?
probes: How would you prove it's a fan-out?

questions.text: An A/B test shows a 3% lift with a p-value of 0.04. What else do you need to know before recommending a launch?
probes: They checked results daily and stopped when it was significant. Problem?

questions.text: Tell me about an analysis you did that changed a decision. How did you present it?
probes: Who disagreed, and how did you handle it?

questions.text: How would you build a model to predict customer churn, and how would you know it's good enough to use?
probes: Churn is 3% of customers. What does that do to accuracy?

questions.text: What is data leakage, and how have you guarded against it?
probes: Give me an example you've actually caught.

questions.text: How would you define an 'active user' for a B2B SaaS product?
probes: How would that definition be gamed?

questions.text: How would you make a daily data pipeline safe to re-run if it fails halfway?
probes: Upstream data arrives late. What now?

questions.text: Explain how a TLS certificate chain is validated, and what happens when an intermediate certificate expires.
strong: correct chain building and failure modes
probes: How would you roll a new intermediate without an outage?

questions.text: You're alerted to unusual outbound traffic from a production server at 2 a.m. What are your first steps?
probes: It's the payments server. Does that change your containment?

questions.text: How would you threat-model a new customer login feature?
probes: Which threat would you fix first and why?

questions.text: A deployment caused errors for 5% of users. How should a deployment pipeline limit and recover from that?
probes: The bad change was a database migration. Now what?

questions.text: How would you reduce a service's cloud bill by 30% without hurting reliability?
probes: Where does the money actually go first?

questions.text: Your project is three weeks behind and the launch date is fixed. What are your options, and how do you choose?
probes: The sponsor refuses scope cuts. Now?

questions.text: How do you identify and track project risks so they don't surprise you?
probes: Tell me about a risk that still surprised you.

questions.text: A large customer's usage dropped 40% over two months and their renewal is in 90 days. What do you do?
probes: Their champion has left the company. Now?

questions.text: An angry client escalates to your CEO about a commitment your team missed. How do you handle the next 48 hours?
strong: owns it and gives a concrete recovery plan
probes: What do you tell your CEO before the call?

questions.text: You take over a business unit that is losing money. What do you do in your first 90 days?
probes: What would you not touch?

questions.text: Tell me about a hard people decision you made that others disagreed with.
probes: Would you make it again?

questions.text: Walk me through a design decision you made that was driven by user research. What did the research show?
probes: What did stakeholders push back on?

questions.text: Sixty percent of users abandon an app's checkout at the payment step. How would you approach redesigning it?
probes: What would you test first?

questions.text: A business team wants to sign a contract today that includes an unlimited liability clause. What do you advise?
probes: The counterparty refuses to change it. Now?

questions.text: A nurse reports a medication error that caused no harm. What should happen next, and why?
probes: How do you encourage people to report near-misses?

questions.text: Walk me through the stages of clinical development for a new drug, and where most programmes fail.
strong: knows why Phase II fails most
probes: What does that mean for a commercial forecast?

questions.text: How would you design a study to test whether a new training programme improves employee productivity?
probes: You can't randomise. What do you do instead?

questions.text: What's something you had to learn quickly for a role or project, and how did you get up to speed?
evidence: how they knew it was enough
probes: How did you decide what to learn first?
How did you know you could rely on it?
What would you do differently?

questions.text: Walk me through a time you changed someone's mind with evidence rather than authority.
probes: What was their view based on?
What evidence moved them?
What did you do when they pushed back?

questions.text: Think of a customer or user whose problem you went out of your way to solve. What did you do, and what did it change?
probes: How did you find out what they really needed?
Was it worth what it cost?
What changed afterwards?

questions.text: What's the best idea you've had that actually got implemented, and how did you get people to adopt it?
probes: Who resisted, and why?
How did you test it first?
How did you measure the result?

questions.text: Describe the best team you've been part of. What did you personally do to make it work?
probes: What did you do that others didn't?
What was hard about that team?
What did you take from it into later teams?

questions.text: What's the biggest setback you've had in your career or studies so far, and what did you do in the first week after it?
probes: What was your part in it?
What did you change afterwards?
How did it affect the next big decision you made?

questions.text: Outside work and studies, what do you spend your time on, and what has it taught you that shows up in how you work?
probes: How did you get into it?
What's the hardest thing you've done in it?
Where does that show up at work?

questions.text: How would the people who've worked closely with you describe you, and what would they say you could do better?
probes: Can you give me an example?
What are you doing about it now?
Who would disagree?

questions.text: What's an achievement outside your job or degree that you're proud of, and what did it take?
probes: What nearly made you stop?
How did you prepare?
What did it teach you?

questions.text: Tell me about something you led that you weren't paid or graded for, like a club, an event or a team. What was hard about it?
probes: What did you personally own?
How did you handle people you couldn't instruct?
What would you do differently?

questions.text: What's something you've taught yourself in the last year, and how did you go about it?
probes: Why that?
How did you know you were improving?
What will you learn next?

questions.text: Pick a recent business news story you've followed closely. What happened, and what would you have done if you were running one of the companies involved?
strong: takes a position with a trade-off
probes: Who wins and who loses from this?
What would you do in the next quarter?
What would change your view?

questions.text: What's one trend changing the industry this role sits in, and which companies do you think win or lose because of it?
probes: Why now?
Who is best placed, and why?
What does it mean for someone in this role?

questions.text: Which company do you think is making a smart strategic move right now, and what's the biggest risk in it?
probes: How would you know it's working?
What would a competitor do in response?
What would you do differently?

questions.text: If you had two minutes to brief a CEO in this industry on one development from the last few months, what would you tell them, and what should they do about it?
questions.intent: Synthesis of current events into advice.
probes: Why that one over the others?
What's the first decision they should make?
What's the risk if they ignore it?
